text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- India is likely to propose demilitarisation of the Siachen glacier by troop pull-backs on both sides.
- A seven-member federal cabinet was sworn in at the presidency in Islamabad.

- Foreign currency accounts in Pakistan will remain fully tax-exempt and depositors will enjoy complete immunity from any inquiry regarding the source of funds, the state's Central Board of Revenue said.
- A Lahore court has abolished two percent service charges on all imports subject to pre-shipment inspection.
- The government has decided to ban import of all luxury items to save foreign exchange.
- The U.S. State Department, worried by the current wave of sectarian violence in Pakistan, has warned its citizens to beef up their security measures.
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan asked private banks to submit several key performance indicators.
- All commercial banks will observe Friday as half working day and Sunday as weekly holiday from this week.
- Pakistan will develop free petroleum port facilities at Gwadar in Balochistan province to cater for needs of other countries in the region, Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said.
- President Farooq Leghari said Pakistan must fully exploit its hydro-electric resources to meet future electricity demand.
- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said a new incentive package for offshore exploration was being developed to attract oil exploration companies.
- The U.S. embassy has decided to reopen its Karachi visa office on March 5. The office was closed after the assassination of two consulate employees in March 1995.
